raw_response:
My family has farmed this land for three generations. My father grew wheat and corn, his father grew wheat and corn, and so will I. The neighbors all do the same — in Quzhou, that is just what the land is for. I have about 10 mu. I know no other way and have no reason to change.

For winter wheat, I will plant around October like every year. I will buy the improved seeds from the village supply store — I do not remember the exact name but I ask the shopkeeper what everyone else is buying and I buy that. I put down plenty of fertilizer in the base dressing, mostly diammonium phosphate and urea, and I top-dress again at jointing. Better to put more than to risk a poor harvest — fertilizer is cheap compared to losing the crop. I will pump water from the well three times: once at planting to get germination, once in winter so the roots do not dry out, once at heading. I spray herbicide once in spring and maybe something for aphids if I see them.

After wheat harvest in June I will plant summer maize immediately. No time to plough properly so I just use the rotary tiller. I throw the seed in, apply urea a couple of times, water once if August is dry. Maize mostly takes care of itself here.

That is the whole year. I will not try cotton or vegetables — I do not know them, I have no contract with any buyer, and if I fail there is nothing to fall back on.
